2. Refund Eligibility Rules
Refund outcomes depend on account dates, product status and entitlement type.
2.1 Initial purchase refunds
 For 30-day policy accounts, the request must fall within 30 calendar days of the first paid start

 Refund eligibility does not automatically imply immediate payment; approval thresholds still

2.2 Duplicate and incorrect charges
A confirmed duplicate charge or billing-system error may be corrected regardless of the standard 
cancellation window. The assistant should distinguish a billing correction from a discretionary 
refund.

3. Service Credits and Incident-Related Adjustments
Service credits are not the same as refunds.
3.1 Credit eligibility
Service credits may apply when a documented service incident breaches the applicable SLA and the 
customer has an entitlement

3.2 Evidence requirements
 Incident ID or verified service-impact record
 Affected account/product
 Impact window
 Applicable SLA tier
 Customer claim or support confirmation
3.3 Credit limits
Standard automated recommendations must not exceed 25% of the affected monthly subscription 
amount. Higher adjustments require finance approval or contract-specific review.

4. Exceptions, Escalation and Fraud Controls
Some requests require manual handling even when they appear policy-compliant.
4.1 Mandatory escalation
 Refund request above $1,000
 More than two refund requests for the same account within 12 months
 Customer disputes ownership or payment authorization
 Contract-specific entitlement but contract language is unavailable
 Potential fraud, chargeback or sanctions concern
4.2 Response language
Do not promise that a refund "will be issued

guage
Do not promise that a refund "will be issued" before approval. Use language such as "appears 
eligible for review" until the required approval is complete.
4.3 Partial evidence
If dates or entitlement status are missing, the assistant should ask for clarification or retrieve 
structured data before making a recommendation.
